SK3050 An exception is thrown out of an async void body

A throw inside an async void method or local function, where nothing between it and the body's edge can catch it.

CategoryAsync
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperAsyncVoidThrowException (resharper_async_void_throw_exception_highlighting)

Why

An async void method has nowhere to put an exception. There is no task to fault, so the compiler-generated builder hands it to whatever SynchronizationContext was captured — and where there is none, which is every console application and every thread-pool callback, that is an unhandled exception on a pool thread and the process ends. The caller's try/catch never sees it, because the caller returned at the first await. A catch that logs and then rethrows is therefore strictly worse than no handler at all: it turns a recorded failure into a terminated process.

Example

Instead of:

async void OnSaveClicked(object sender, EventArgs e) {
    try {
        await SaveAsync();
    } catch (IOException ex) {
        logger.LogError(ex, "save failed");
        throw;
    }
}

Write:

async void OnSaveClicked(object sender, EventArgs e) {
    try {
        await SaveAsync();
    } catch (IOException ex) {
        logger.LogError(ex, "save failed");
        ShowError(ex);
    }
}

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ The export sets resharper_async_void_throw_exception_highlighting = suggestion and this rule defaults to warning. ReSharper files it under "Potential Code Quality Issues"; the consequence is not potential and not a quality issue — an exception on a captured context with no handler ends the process — and doc 00's ninth non-negotiable takes a severity from what the rule means rather than from what the reference tool set. Reading the ReSharper key (off by default, doc 03 § "Severities") would demote it to suggestion.

When it does not fire

⚠ Event handlers are reported, and that is the decision rather than an oversight. SK3001 excludes them because its remedy — return Task — is not available to a method whose signature an event declares. This rule's remedy is different and is available to every async void there is: handle the exception where it is thrown. Excluding handlers would exclude the one place async void is legitimate and therefore the place this defect actually reaches production. ⚠ Lambdas are not matched at all, which is what makes the rule disjoint from SK3052 by construction: an async lambda converted to a void delegate is async void too, and it is reported once, at the conversion, by SK3052 — which is where the remedy is. The owner must be a declaration that writes void in its own source. ⚠ A `throw` an enclosing `try` in the same body could catch is not reported, and the test is deliberately over-broad: any catch at all on an enclosing try silences the finding, even one whose filter could not possibly match. A throw written inside a catch clause is not silenced by that clause's own try, because the clause it is written in does not catch it — that rethrow is the shape the rule exists for. Test methods are excluded for the same reason SK3002 excludes them, and generated code is excluded. No fix is offered: deleting the throw swallows the exception, wrapping the body changes what the method does, and turning the method into async Task is SK3001's edit and a caller-wide refactor. The finding is true and the repair is a decision.
